text:
BySiladitya Ray,

Forbes Staff.

President Donald Trump on Wednesday said the interim peace deal with Iran is “over” as he described the country’s leaders as “sick people” while speaking to reporters at the NATO summit in Turkey, where he also blasted members of the alliance for not backing him in the war with Tehran.

Speaking to reporters alongside NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Trump was asked whether the memorandum of understanding that the two sides agreed to last month was dead, and he replied, “To me, I think it's over.”

The president said he doesn’t want to deal with Iran’s leaders anymore, as he labeled them as “scum” and said, “they're vicious, violent people.”

Referring to Khamenei’s funeral, Trump said the U.S. told the Iranians to go ahead and do the funeral, but instead of that, they started “shooting rockets at ships.”

Trump said he will speak to the U.S. negotiators, and noted it’s “a waste of time” dealing with Iran.

The president accused Iranian officials of engaging in double speak with regard to the negotiations and claimed that they would agree to a deal on matters like no nuclear weapons behind closed doors, and then say something opposite to the press.

When asked if he may be open to the resumption of talks, the president says he doesn’t care, “they can talk…I think they're wasting their time.”

Threats of a resumed conflict and potential disruption in the Strait of Hormuz triggered a surge in global crude oil prices, with the benchmark Brent Crude Futures index surging above $79 a barrel, up from around $72 at the start of this week.

U.S. stock futures fell sharply on Wednesday after Trump declared an end to the ceasefire. The benchmark S&P 500 futures dropped more than 1% to 7,472.25 points, while down futures fell 1.3% to 52,506 points. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Futures were also hit hard, dropping 1.5% to 28,941 points. Key indices in Europe and Asia also saw sharp slumps.

Aside from expressing anger and frustration over Iran, Trump called out other members of the NATO alliance while seated next to Rutte. The president told reporters: “I’m not happy with NATO because of what they did with Greenland, and I’m not happy with NATO because of the fact that they didn’t want to help us with the number one state sponsor of terror, that’s Iran. They were unwilling to help us.” Spain emerged as the main target of Trump’s ire as the president declared the country as a “wasted cause.” Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sánchez has become one of the most vocal critics among Western leaders of Trump’s war with Iran. Trump called Spain a “terrible partner” alleging that: “They don’t participate. They don’t pay. I don’t want anything to do with Spain. Cut off all trade with Spain, please, including visits.”

On Tuesday, the U.S. military’s Central Command launched major strikes against Iran in retaliation against attacks on commercial ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has since retaliated by launching attacks on Gulf neighbors housing U.S. military bases. In a statement, CENTCOM said the strikes on Iran were meant to “impose heavy costs for targeting and attacking commercial shipping crewed by innocent civilians.” The White House also revoked a 60-day waiver on sanctions against Iran that allowed the country to freely sell its oil in the international market.

U.S. Begins ‘Powerful’ Strikes Against Iran Over Strait Of Hormuz Ship Attacks (Forbes)
